sections.name: body
sections.value:
Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR: #148
Head: 5de084c74c75ea63532bec6f4eb36a9f872092d7
Scope: the PR-owned commits against merge base 27efa69ced77776e3a25b990c68aa790c3f518bf; main's imported changes excluded. No high-confidence exploitable security vulnerability found.

Trust boundaries:
- AC3's early native-session conflict check is veto-only. It avoids host observation for a known conflict without granting admission or replacing the lock-time check. The existing machine-bearer boundary already permits roster and known-address state reads; this is not a new unauthenticated address-probing surface. The zero-observation refusal test has a positive observation control.
- AC1's client attempt strings become enums, never retained raw labels. attempts.rs:53-62 normalizes recognized, missing and arbitrary labels; enum-tuple storage at :167-170 limits combinations to 10 paths x 2 modes x 9 outcomes = 180. Snapshot keys use static spellings (:208-215), at most 35 rendered bytes. Arbitrary client labels cannot create counter-key cardinality or shell/path injection.
- Seat retention is at most 64 named addresses plus overflow (attempts.rs:18-21,193-199). Ping and registration remain bearer-authenticated (http/mod.rs:725-761); paired-peer credentials cannot access either endpoint through the peer allowlist (:418-424).
- AC4's terminal stop is restricted to HTTP 400, v2, ok:false, /v1/register, E-RS-SEAT-RETIRED. The idempotent receive hold aborts both loops and reports once. Discriminator negative controls preserve other-refusal and healthy lease/backoff behavior.

Notes and limitations:
1. Cardinality is not a small retained-byte bound. record() accepts an unrestricted address string, and admission rejects blank IDs without imposing a length cap (core admission.rs:122-147). register_via records the original claimed string on service errors (registration.rs:130-187), so rejected claims can enter the retained map. The HTTP JSON extractor has Axum's separate default 2 MiB body limit, making 64 near-limit direct claims approach 128 MiB of retained address bytes. No universal retained-byte ceiling is established for internal/resolved addresses. This is an availability/hardening caveat, not proof of an unauthorized exploit.
2. Ping newly exposes bounded historical/refused claim strings and tallies (http/mod.rs:819-826) to existing machine-bearer holders. It does not expose raw attempt labels, registration bodies, credentials or error text. Treat claimed addresses as non-sensitive identifiers; the review does not claim zero new data visibility.
3. Correctness and performance independently BLOCK this head for accounting gaps: early HTTP refusals bypass counting, startup/standby reasons are mislabelled, and a late macOS blocking observer can pay ps after its attempt tally was finalized. This security verdict does not clear those blocks.
4. AC2's live attribution after deployment and tk-0004/tk-0005 remain explicitly deferred. No live cost/attribution proof is claimed.

Evidence:
- Exact-head CI run 42351634792 is completed SUCCESS: https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42351634792
- Exact-head body-edited Delivers run 42352055393 is completed SUCCESS: https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42352055393
- GitHub reports CLEAN and all reported checks successful. The worktree was reviewed clean at the pinned head.
- No local builds/tests, runtime probes, credential-file inspection or worktree mutation. CI is Linux-only; the changed macOS observer remains source-assessed rather than compiled/executed by this CI evidence.
